--- START OF SOURCE: jacobi-2d.c ---
/**

 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>

/* jacobi-2d.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "jacobi-2d.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      {
	A[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*(j+2) + 2) / n;
	B[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*(j+3) + 3) / n;
      }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_jacobi_2d[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps,
			    int n,
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (t = 0; t < _PB_TSTEPS; t++)
    {
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  B[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][1+j] + A[1+i][j] + A[i-1][j]);
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  A[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][1+j] + B[1+i][j] + B[i-1][j]);
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_jacobi_2d(tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

--- END OF SOURCE: jacobi-2d.c ---

--- START OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-01 ---
domain:
    # Global problem sizes
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)        # time iteration (each iteration = 2 Jacobi sweeps)
    i: dim in [0, N)             # space, row index
    j: dim in [0, N)             # space, column index

    # Interior region where the stencil is applied
    ii: dim in [1, N-1)          # interior rows
    jj: dim in [1, N-1)          # interior columns

data:
    # 2D grids, row-major layout
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # A is both input and output:
        # - boundaries i ∈ {0, N-1} or j ∈ {0, N-1} are initialized once and never updated
        # - interior ii, jj is updated at every time step
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # B is a temporary ping-pong buffer:
        # - boundaries same as for A: initialized and never updated
        # - interior holds intermediate Jacobi values between the two sweeps in each t

parameters:
    N:       int                  # grid size (same in both dimensions)
    TSTEPS:  int                  # number of outer iterations in the original code
    w:       DATA_TYPE            # stencil weight, w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tunable performance parameters (no effect on numerical semantics):
    TI:      int                  # tile size in i (rows), e.g., 32 or 64
    TJ:      int                  # tile size in j (cols), e.g., 64 or 128
    VJ:      int                  # vector width (elements processed per SIMD op), e.g., 4, 8
    UJ:      int                  # unroll factor for j, e.g., 2, 4

computation:
    # Precompute scalar weight once, outside time loop
    C0: w = w

    # Time loop is strictly sequential: each t depends on t-1 via A
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        #------------------------------------------
        # Sweep 1: Jacobi update from A^t to B^t
        #   B[i,j] = w * ( A[i,j] + A[i,j-1] + A[i,j+1] + A[i-1,j] + A[i+1,j] )
        #------------------------------------------
        S1:
            for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
                B[ii, jj] =
                    C0 * ( A[ii,   jj  ] +
                           A[ii,   jj-1] +
                           A[ii,   jj+1] +
                           A[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           A[ii+1, jj  ] )

        #------------------------------------------
        # Sweep 2: Jacobi update from B^t to A^(t+1)
        #   A[i,j] = w * ( B[i,j] + B[i,j-1] + B[i,j+1] + B[i-1,j] + B[i+1,j] )
        #------------------------------------------
        S2:
            for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
                A[ii, jj] =
                    C0 * ( B[ii,   jj  ] +
                           B[ii,   jj-1] +
                           B[ii,   jj+1] +
                           B[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           B[ii+1, jj  ] )

dependencies:
    # 1. Within a given time step t, all S1 updates must complete before any S2 update:
    #    (matches the two separate for-loops in the original C code)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS):
        for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
            S1(t, ii, jj) -> S2(t, *, *)

    # 2. Across time steps, new A produced by S2 at time t is the input A for S1 at time t+1:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        S2(t, *, *) -> S1(t+1, *, *)

    # 3. There are no loop-carried dependencies along ii or jj *within* a sweep:
    #    each point only reads from the previous array (A for S1, B for S2),
    #    and writes to a distinct element in the target array.
    #    This allows full parallelization in the spatial dimensions per sweep.

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Spatial blocking (tiling) to improve cache reuse
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D spatial domain for both sweeps:
    #   - I and J are tile indices
    #   - ii and jj (interior indices) become intra-tile indices
    block(ii, I, TI)      # ii = I * TI + local_ii, tiles of TI rows
    block(jj, J, TJ)      # jj = J * TJ + local_jj, tiles of TJ cols

    # Hoist tile loops to just inside the time loop, so entire tiles are
    # processed for S1, then entire tiles for S2, preserving S1->S2 ordering.
    hoist(I)              # place I as the outermost spatial loop (after t)
    hoist(J)              # place J as next outer spatial loop

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (I, J) tile in a given sweep and time step is independent:
    # we can process tiles in parallel both in S1 and S2.
    # On a 32-core x64 machine, TI×TJ is chosen so that one or a few tiles
    # fit comfortably into L2 / L3 per core.
    parallelize(I)        # distribute tiles across threads
    # (J remains inside I; larger TJ gives good work per tile and contiguous memory)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMD vectorization along the innermost dimension
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # jj indexes contiguous memory (row-major), so we vectorize along jj.
    # VJ should match the hardware SIMD width, e.g., 4 for AVX2 float, 8 for AVX2 double.
    vectorize(jj, VJ)     # emit vector loads/stores and fused adds for stencil in j

    # Optional loop unrolling in j to reduce loop overhead and expose ILP
    unroll(jj, UJ)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic and scalar optimizations
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    #  - The constant weight 0.2 (C0) is hoisted out of all loops.
    #  - Compilers can fuse additions and multiplication into FMA instructions
    #    where available, especially under -O3.
    #  - No change to the mathematical stencil; only the evaluation order within
    #    each sum may change, causing at most benign floating-point roundoff differences.
    hoist(C0)             # ensure 'w' is computed/loaded once outside the time-space loops

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Layout and memory access
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # We *keep* row-major layout for both A and B; the innermost jj loop traverses
    # contiguous elements, yielding:
    #   - unit-stride loads/stores for A[ii,*] and B[ii,*]
    #   - regular strided accesses for neighbors in i (ii-1, ii+1)
    #
    # Changing to column-major would harm the primary access pattern in jj,
    # so we explicitly preserve row-major layout and rely on spatial blocking
    # plus caches to amortize the strided accesses in ii.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-02 ---
domain:
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)   # time steps
    i: dim in [0, N)        # space, row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # space, column index

data:
    # Row-major 2D arrays matching C layout: A[i][j] and B[i][j]
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # live-in and live-out
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # used as ping-pong buffer; initial contents unused

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of Jacobi time steps
    omega: DATA_TYPE        # relaxation coefficient, = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tunable performance parameters (chosen w.r.t. cache / SIMD of the target)
    TI: int                 # tile size in i (e.g., 32–256)
    TJ: int                 # tile size in j (e.g., 64–512, multiple of VEC_J)
    VEC_J: int              # SIMD vector width along j (elements)
    UNROLL_J: int           # unroll factor for inner j-loop

computation:
    # 2D Jacobi with 5-point stencil, double-buffered in A and B.
    # Boundary points (i==0, i==N-1, j==0, j==N-1) are never updated.
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):      # time loop must remain sequential
        # Phase 1: B := Jacobi(A)
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S1: B[i, j] =
                    omega * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                              A[i,   j-1] +
                              A[i,   j+1] +
                              A[i-1, j  ] +
                              A[i+1, j  ] )

        # Phase 2: A := Jacobi(B)
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S2: A[i, j] =
                    omega * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                              B[i,   j-1] +
                              B[i,   j+1] +
                              B[i-1, j  ] +
                              B[i+1, j  ] )

optimization:
    # Assumptions:
    # - A and B are distinct, non-aliasing row-major buffers.
    # - N is large so the interior dominates.
    # - N, TSTEPS, omega and tile / SIMD parameters are invariant inside the kernel.

    # 1. Spatial blocking (tiling) over i and j to improve cache locality.
    #    Applied identically to both S1 and S2; boundaries are handled by
    #    clipping tile ranges to [1, N-1).
    block(i, II, TI)        # split i into outer tile index II and inner i
    block(j, JJ, TJ)        # split j into outer tile index JJ and inner j

    # Resulting per-time-step structure (conceptually):
    #   for II                          # tiles of rows
    #     for JJ                        # tiles of columns
    #       for i in tile(II) ∩ [1,N-1)
    #         for j in tile(JJ) ∩ [1,N-1)

    # 2. Loop ordering:
    #    - Keep t outermost and sequential.
    #    - Within each time step, iterate over tiles first (II, JJ),
    #      then intra-tile i, then intra-tile j (unit-stride).
    hoist(t)                # t already outermost; make this explicit
    hoist(II)               # tile rows outside tile columns
    hoist(JJ)               # tile columns outside intra-tile loops

    # 3. Parallelization:
    #    - Within a fixed (t, phase), all (i,j) updates are independent.
    #    - Parallelize on the outer row tiles to reduce scheduling overhead
    #      and balance work across cores.
    parallelize(II)         # distribute II-tiles across threads for S1 and S2

    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling:
    #    - j is the innermost loop and contiguous in memory (row-major),
    #      so vectorize along j.
    #    - Choose TJ as a multiple of VEC_J to minimize scalar remainder work.
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)     # map inner j loop to SIMD lanes
    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)     # unroll j loop within each vectorized chunk

    # 5. Scalar / arithmetic hoisting:
    #    - Keep omega in a register at the innermost level.
    #    - Allow the compiler to use fused multiply-add for omega * sum5.
    hoist(omega)            # load omega once per (t, II, JJ) region (or wider)
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-03 ---
domain:
    # Time dimension (Jacobi iterations; each iteration performs two 5-point sweeps)
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # Spatial dimensions restricted to the interior points actually updated
    # (grid is N x N, but i=0, i=N-1, j=0, j=N-1 are fixed boundary values)
    i: dim in [1, N-1)
    j: dim in [1, N-1)

data:
    # 2D grids stored in row-major order (C layout)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Note: memory for A and B is actually allocated for i,j in [0, N),
    # but only interior indices [1, N-1) are written in the kernel.
    # Boundary rows/columns (i=0, i=N-1, j=0, j=N-1) remain at their
    # initialized values and are only read as neighbors.

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid size in each spatial dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of time steps (each step = 2 sweeps)
    w: DATA_TYPE            # stencil weight; w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tuning parameters for optimization (chosen based on hardware/cache)
    TI: int                 # tile size in the i (row) dimension, e.g., 32..256
    VF: int                 # SIMD vector length for j, e.g., 4 or 8
    U: int                  # unrolling factor for j, typically a multiple of VF

computation:
    # For each time step t, perform:
    #   1) A -> B 5-point Jacobi sweep on interior points
    #   2) B -> A 5-point Jacobi sweep on interior points
    #
    # Time steps must execute sequentially because each uses the result
    # of the previous one.
    for t in seq[0, TSTEPS):
        # Sweep 1: read A, write B
        for i, j:
            JACOBI_B(t, i, j):
                B[i, j] =
                    w * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                          A[i,   j-1] +
                          A[i,   j+1] +
                          A[i-1, j  ] +
                          A[i+1, j  ] )

        # Sweep 2: read B, write A
        for i, j:
            JACOBI_A(t, i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    w * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                          B[i,   j-1] +
                          B[i,   j+1] +
                          B[i-1, j  ] +
                          B[i+1, j  ] )

dependencies:
    # Within a given time step t, each interior point (i, j) in sweep 2
    # depends on its 5-point neighborhood in B from sweep 1 of the same t.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i, j:
        # Direct center dependency (neighborhood dependencies are implicit)
        JACOBI_B(t, i, j) -> JACOBI_A(t, i, j)

    # Across time steps, A at time t+1 is produced by JACOBI_A(t, ·, ·)
    # and used as input to JACOBI_B(t+1, ·, ·). This enforces that the
    # outer time loop remains sequential.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1), i, j:
        JACOBI_A(t, i, j) -> JACOBI_B(t+1, i, j)

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Preserve row-major friendly access and innermost j-loop
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The kernel already iterates with j as the innermost loop, which
    # matches row-major storage (elements with consecutive j are contiguous).
    # We keep this structure to maximize spatial locality and enable SIMD.
    hoist(t)  # keep t as the outermost loop (no-op but documented)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization over row tiles (multi-core scalability)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (t, i, j) update within a sweep only reads from the "old" array
    # (A for JACOBI_B, B for JACOBI_A) and writes to the "new" one, so
    # there are no loop-carried dependencies along i or j inside a sweep.
    #
    # We tile the i dimension into blocks of TI consecutive rows and
    # parallelize over the outer tile index. This:
    #   - gives each thread a large, cache-friendly chunk of rows,
    #   - reduces scheduling overhead vs. per-row parallelism,
    #   - maintains correctness because different i-tiles are independent.
    block(i, ii, TI)       # i = ii * TI + (inner i in [0, TI) with bounds clipping)
    hoist(ii)              # loop order: for t, for ii, for i-in-tile, for j
    parallelize(ii)        # run row tiles in parallel for each sweep & time step

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization and unrolling along j
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost j-loop accesses:
    #   A[i, j], A[i, j±1], A[i±1, j]   (or the same pattern on B)
    # which are all at small, fixed offsets. This is ideal for auto-
    # vectorization. We make this explicit and allow the vector width
    # and unroll factor to be tuned.
    vectorize(j, VF)       # map j-iterations to SIMD lanes (e.g., AVX2/AVX-512)
    unroll(j, U)           # unroll j-loop to increase ILP and hide latencies

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic simplifications (kept implicit)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The expression is already in the form:
    #   tmp = A/B neighbors sum
    #   out = w * tmp
    # so a single multiplication by w per point is required.
    # Modern compilers will:
    #   - hoist the constant w = 0.2 outside loops,
    #   - keep partial sums in registers.
    # No additional arithmetic restructuring is necessary in the model.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Optional refinement: per-tile software prefetching (comment-only)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # On very large grids where N is much larger than the last-level cache,
    # a further micro-optimization is to add software prefetches for the
    # next rows of A (in JACOBI_B) and B (in JACOBI_A) within each tile ii.
    # This can be modeled as:
    #   #prefetch(A[i+Δ, j]) and #prefetch(B[i+Δ, j])
    # for some small Δ (e.g., 2–4), but is left as an implementation choice
    # rather than a formal directive here.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-04 ---
domain:
    # Time dimension: tsteps outer loop is strictly sequential
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # Space dimensions: N x N grid
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Row-major 2D arrays: contiguous in j
    # index(i, j) = i * N + j
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Only interior points [1, N-1) x [1, N-1) are updated.
    # Boundary values A[0,*], A[N-1,*], A[* ,0], A[* ,N-1] remain as initialized
    # and are read as fixed Dirichlet boundaries throughout the computation.

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid size in each dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of outer iterations
    w: DATA_TYPE            # Jacobi weight, w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) in code

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int                 # spatial tile size in i (rows), e.g., 32–128
    TJ: int                 # spatial tile size in j (cols), e.g., 32–256
    VEC: int                # vector width for j (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)

computation:
    # For each time step, perform two Jacobi sweeps:
    #  1. B <- stencil(A)
    #  2. A <- stencil(B)
    #
    # Time is strictly sequential to match original semantics and FP behavior.
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):

        # First sweep: compute B from A at time t
        # Matches:
        #   B[i][j] = 0.2 * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][j+1]
        #                    + A[i+1][j] + A[i-1][j]);
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S1_B_from_A(t, i, j):
                B[i, j] =
                    w * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                          A[i,   j-1] +
                          A[i,   j+1] +
                          A[i+1, j  ] +
                          A[i-1, j  ] )

        # Second sweep: compute A from B at the same time step
        # Matches:
        #   A[i][j] = 0.2 * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][j+1]
        #                    + B[i+1][j] + B[i-1][j]);
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S2_A_from_B(t, i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    w * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                          B[i,   j-1] +
                          B[i,   j+1] +
                          B[i+1, j  ] +
                          B[i-1, j  ] )

dependencies:
    # Within a given time step t, each A-update depends on the corresponding
    # B-updates of the same step.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        S1_B_from_A(t, i, j) -> S2_A_from_B(t, i, j)

    # Across time steps, A at step t is the input state for computing B at t+1.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        S2_A_from_B(t, i, j) -> S1_B_from_A(t+1, i, j)

optimization:
    # ---- Spatial blocking (tiling) for cache locality ----
    # We tile i and j so that sub-blocks of A and B fit better into caches.
    # This preserves semantics because tiles are processed in a way that
    # respects the original order within each full sweep.
    block(i, ii, TI)     # i = ii * TI + i_in_tile
    block(j, jj, TJ)     # j = jj * TJ + j_in_tile

    # Keep time dimension outermost; sweeps remain ordered as in original code.
    hoist(t)

    # Apply tiling separately to both sweeps inside each time step:
    #   for t:
    #     for ii, jj: tile of B-from-A
    #     for ii, jj: tile of A-from-B
    #
    # B tiles for a given time step are fully computed (global barrier implied)
    # before any A tiles of that step are used, preserving:
    #   "finish all B updates at t before any A update at t".
    hoist(ii)
    hoist(jj)

    # ---- Parallelization ----
    # Each (i, j) update within a sweep depends only on neighbor values
    # from the *input* grid of that sweep, which is read-only in that phase.
    # Therefore, the spatial loops are safe to parallelize.
    #
    # We parallelize at the outer tile level to:
    #  - amortize thread-management overhead,
    #  - avoid false sharing on adjacent rows/cols,
    #  - map well onto a 32-core CPU (many tiles in flight).
    parallelize(ii)      # distribute tiles of rows across threads
    # Optionally also:

static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");

    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_jacobi_2d[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps,
			    int n,
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (t = 0; t < _PB_TSTEPS; t++)
    {
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  B[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][1+j] + A[1+i][j] + A[i-1][j]);
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  A[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][1+j] + B[1+i][j] + B[i-1][j]);
    }
#pragma endscop

}

  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

                           A[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           A[ii+1, jj  ] )

        #   A[i,j] = w * ( B[i,j] + B[i,j-1] + B[i,j+1] + B[i-1,j] + B[i+1,j] )

    #   - reduces scheduling overhead vs. per-row parallelism,
    #   - maintains correctness because different i-tiles are independent.
    block(i, ii, TI)       # i = ii * TI + (inner i in [0, TI) with bounds clipping)
    hoist(ii)              # loop order: for t, for ii, for i-in-tile, for j
    parallelize(ii)        # run row tiles in parallel for each sweep & time step

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization and unrolling along j
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost j-loop accesses:
    #   A[i, j], A[i, j±1], A[i±1, j]   (or the same pattern on B)
    # which are all at small, fixed offsets. This is ideal for auto-
    # vectorization. We make this explicit and allow the vector width
    # and unroll factor to be tuned.
    vectorize(j, VF)       # map j-iterations to SIMD lanes (e.g., AVX2/AVX-512)
    unroll(j, U)           # unroll j-loop to increase ILP and hide latencies

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic simplifications (kept implicit)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The expression is already in the form:
    #   tmp = A/B neighbors sum
    #   out = w * tmp
    # so a single multiplication by w per point is required.
    # Modern compilers will:
    #   - hoist the constant w = 0.2 outside loops,
    #   - keep partial sums in registers.
    # No additional arithmetic restructuring is necessary in the model.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Optional refinement: per-tile software prefetching (comment-only)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # On very large grids where N is much larger than the last-level cache,
    # a further micro-optimization is to add software prefetches for the
    # next rows of A (in JACOBI_B) and B (in JACOBI_A) within each tile ii.
    # This can be modeled as:
    #   #prefetch(A[i+Δ, j]) and #prefetch(B[i+Δ, j])
    # for some small Δ (e.g., 2–4), but is left as an implementation choice
    # rather than a formal directive here.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-03 ---

domain:
    # Time dimension: tsteps outer loop is strictly sequential
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # Space dimensions: N x N grid
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Row-major 2D arrays: contiguous in j
    # index(i, j) = i * N + j
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Only interior points [1, N-1) x [1, N-1) are updated.
    # Boundary values A[0,*], A[N-1,*], A[* ,0], A[* ,N-1] remain as initialized
    # and are read as fixed Dirichlet boundaries throughout the computation.

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid size in each dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of outer iterations
    w: DATA_TYPE            # Jacobi weight, w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) in code

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int                 # spatial tile size in i (rows), e.g., 32–128
    TJ: int                 # spatial tile size in j (cols), e.g., 32–256
    VEC: int                # vector width for j (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)

computation:
    # For each time step, perform two Jacobi sweeps:
    #  1. B <- stencil(A)
    #  2. A <- stencil(B)
    #
    # Time is strictly sequential to match original semantics and FP behavior.
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):

        # First sweep: compute B from A at time t
        # Matches:
        #   B[i][j] = 0.2 * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][j+1]
        #                    + A[i+1][j] + A[i-1][j]);
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S1_B_from_A(t, i, j):
                B[i, j] =
                    w * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                          A[i,   j-1] +
                          A[i,   j+1] +
                          A[i+1, j  ] +
                          A[i-1, j  ] )

        # Second sweep: compute A from B at the same time step
        # Matches:
        #   A[i][j] = 0.2 * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][j+1]
        #                    + B[i+1][j] + B[i-1][j]);
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S2_A_from_B(t, i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    w * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                          B[i,   j-1] +
                          B[i,   j+1] +
                          B[i+1, j  ] +
                          B[i-1, j  ] )

dependencies:
    # Within a given time step t, each A-update depends on the corresponding
    # B-updates of the same step.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        S1_B_from_A(t, i, j) -> S2_A_from_B(t, i, j)

    # Across time steps, A at step t is the input state for computing B at t+1.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        S2_A_from_B(t, i, j) -> S1_B_from_A(t+1, i, j)

optimization:
    # ---- Spatial blocking (tiling) for cache locality ----
    # We tile i and j so that sub-blocks of A and B fit better into caches.
    # This preserves semantics because tiles are processed in a way that
    # respects the original order within each full sweep.
    block(i, ii, TI)     # i = ii * TI + i_in_tile
    block(j, jj, TJ)     # j = jj * TJ + j_in_tile

    # Keep time dimension outermost; sweeps remain ordered as in original code.
    hoist(t)

    # Apply tiling separately to both sweeps inside each time step:
    #   for t:
    #     for ii, jj: tile of B-from-A
    #     for ii, jj: tile of A-from-B
    #
    # B tiles for a given time step are fully computed (global barrier implied)
    # before any A tiles of that step are used, preserving:
    #   "finish all B updates at t before any A update at t".
    hoist(ii)
    hoist(jj)

    # ---- Parallelization ----
    # Each (i, j) update within a sweep depends only on neighbor values
    # from the *input* grid of that sweep, which is read-only in that phase.
    # Therefore, the spatial loops are safe to parallelize.
    #
    # We parallelize at the outer tile level to:
    #  - amortize thread-management overhead,
    #  - avoid false sharing on adjacent rows/cols,
    #  - map well onto a 32-core CPU (many tiles in flight).
    parallelize(ii)      # distribute tiles of rows across threads
    # Optionally also:
    # parallelize(jj)    # if many cores and large N, 2D tile parallelism

    # Time loop t remains sequential: there are true dependencies between
    # successive timesteps and between S1 and S2 at a given t.

    # ---- Vectorization along j ----
    # j is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), and the stencil
    # in j-direction has unit stride. This is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # ---- Loop unrolling ----
    # Unroll the innermost j loop to:
    #  - expose more ILP,
    #  - reduce loop-control overhead,
    #  - help the compiler schedule loads of neighboring points.
    unroll(j, 4)

    # Optional: mild unrolling in time to increase ILP while respecting
    # sequential time semantics (compiler will emit code for two t-steps
    # inlined, but still ordered).
    unroll(t, 2)

    # ---- Arithmetic hoisting ----
    # The scalar weight w = 0.2 is invariant across all loops.
    # Ensure it is loaded once into a register and reused:
    hoist(w)
    # (This corresponds to computing SCALAR_VAL(0.2) once before
    #  entering the time-stepping loops.)

    # ---- Notes on correctness ----
    # - Boundaries (i = 0 or N-1, j = 0 or N-1) are never written,
    #   exactly as in the original code; they are read as fixed values.
    # - No change is made to the stencil formula or to the ordering
    #   between:
    #       B <- A   and   A <- B
    #   within each time step.
    # - All time steps t are executed in order; no reordering across t.
    # - Parallelization and vectorization affect only independent
    #   (i, j) iterations within each sweep, preserving semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-04 ---

domain:
    # Interior grid points only; boundary rows/cols 0 and N-1 remain unchanged.
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)
    i: dim in [1, N-1)
    j: dim in [1, N-1)

data:
    # Full N×N grids stored in row-major order.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major, includes boundaries at indices 0 and N-1
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major, used as a ping-pong buffer

parameters:
    N: int                  # Grid size (both dimensions)
    TSTEPS: int             # Number of outer loop iterations in the original code
    w: DATA_TYPE            # Relaxation weight; in the given code w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)
    TI: int                 # Tunable tile size in the i (row) dimension
    TJ: int                 # Tunable tile size in the j (column) dimension
    VEC_WIDTH: int          # Target vector width (elements) for vectorization over j
    UNROLL_J: int           # Unroll factor for inner j loop

computation:
    # Jacobi 2D stencil with two sweeps per outer time iteration:
    #   1) B = J(A)
    #   2) A = J(B)
    # Boundaries of A and B (i=0 or i=N-1 or j=0 or j=N-1) are never updated.

    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        # Sweep 1: read from A, write to B.
        A_to_B:
            for i, j:
                B[i, j] = w * (
                              A[i,   j  ] +
                              A[i,   j-1] +
                              A[i,   j+1] +
                              A[i-1, j  ] +
                              A[i+1, j  ]
                          )

        # Sweep 2: read from B, write to A.
        B_to_A:
            for i, j:
                A[i, j] = w * (
                              B[i,   j  ] +
                              B[i,   j-1] +
                              B[i,   j+1] +
                              B[i-1, j  ] +
                              B[i+1, j  ]
                          )

optimization:
    # --- Scalar and aliasing assumptions ------------------------------------
    hoist(w)
    # hoist(S): treat scalar S as loop-invariant and hoist its load/definition
    # outside all loops that use it. Here, w = 0.2 is a constant; ensure it is
    # computed/loaded once, not per iteration.

    assume_no_alias(A, B)
    # assume_no_alias(X, Y): X and Y do not alias in memory. This matches the
    # benchmark intent and enables better vectorization and reordering.

    # --- Spatial blocking for cache locality --------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D interior domain (i, j) to improve cache reuse within each
    # sweep. Each tile operates on a small sub-block of the grid.
    block(i, ii, TI)
    block(j, jj, TJ)
    # block(d, D, S): replace loop over dimension d by an outer tile loop D and
    # an inner loop over d with tile size S. For example:
    #   for i in [1, N-1)  -->
    #     for ii in [1, N-1) step TI:
    #       for i in [ii, min(ii+TI, N-1))
    #
    # TI, TJ should be tuned so that a tile of A and B plus its 1-cell halo
    # fits comfortably in L1/L2 cache.

    # --- Parallelization -----------------------------------------------------
    parallelize(ii)
    # parallelize(D): iterations along tile dimension D can be executed in
    # parallel (e.g., via OpenMP). Each time-step t is sequential, but within
    # a time-step, tiles in ii are independent in a Jacobi sweep, so they can
    # be distributed across cores on the 32-core machine.

    # To increase parallelism further for very large N, one can also
    # parallelize over jj in addition to ii, as long as the runtime partitions
    # tiles to avoid excessive synchronization:
    # parallelize(jj)

    # --- Vectorization and unrolling ----------------------------------------
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)
    # vectorize(d, W): enforce SIMD vectorization along dimension d with width W.
    # Here, inner j is contiguous in row-major layout, so vector loads/stores
    # for A[i, j±1] and B[i, j±1] are naturally aligned and efficient.

    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)
    # unroll(d, F): unroll loop d by factor F to reduce loop overhead and allow
    # the compiler to better schedule loads, adds, and the final multiply by w.

    # --- Loop ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    # Preserve the original nesting order (t outer, then i, then j) to ensure
    # correctness of the time-dependent stencil and to keep j innermost for
    # vectorization and unit-stride memory access:
    #   t (sequential) -> ii (parallel tiles) -> jj -> i -> j (vectorized)
    #
    # No interchange of t with spatial dimensions is allowed because each
    # time-step depends on the previous one.

    # --- Optional: time-iteration unrolling (purely local) -------------------
    # The outer time loop can be unrolled by a small factor (e.g., 2) to expose
    # more ILP, without changing the number of stencil applications:
    # unroll(t, 2)
    # This preserves semantics because iterations of t are strictly sequential
    # but can still be mechanically unrolled by the compiler.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-05 ---

#include <stdio.h>

#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "jacobi-2d.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      {
	A[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*(j+2) + 2) / n;
	B[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*(j+3) + 3) / n;
      }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_jacobi_2d[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps,
			    int n,
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (t = 0; t < _PB_TSTEPS; t++)
    {
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  B[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][1+j] + A[1+i][j] + A[i-1][j]);
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  A[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][1+j] + B[1+i][j] + B[i-1][j]);
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_jacobi_2d(tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)        # time iteration (each iteration = 2 Jacobi sweeps)
    i: dim in [0, N)             # space, row index
    j: dim in [0, N)             # space, column index

    # Interior region where the stencil is applied
    ii: dim in [1, N-1)          # interior rows
    jj: dim in [1, N-1)          # interior columns

data:
    # 2D grids, row-major layout
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # A is both input and output:
        # - boundaries i ∈ {0, N-1} or j ∈ {0, N-1} are initialized once and never updated
        # - interior ii, jj is updated at every time step
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
        # B is a temporary ping-pong buffer:
        # - boundaries same as for A: initialized and never updated
        # - interior holds intermediate Jacobi values between the two sweeps in each t

parameters:
    N:       int                  # grid size (same in both dimensions)
    TSTEPS:  int                  # number of outer iterations in the original code
    w:       DATA_TYPE            # stencil weight, w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tunable performance parameters (no effect on numerical semantics):
    TI:      int                  # tile size in i (rows), e.g., 32 or 64
    TJ:      int                  # tile size in j (cols), e.g., 64 or 128
    VJ:      int                  # vector width (elements processed per SIMD op), e.g., 4, 8
    UJ:      int                  # unroll factor for j, e.g., 2, 4

computation:
    # Precompute scalar weight once, outside time loop
    C0: w = w

    # Time loop is strictly sequential: each t depends on t-1 via A
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        #------------------------------------------
        # Sweep 1: Jacobi update from A^t to B^t
        #   B[i,j] = w * ( A[i,j] + A[i,j-1] + A[i,j+1] + A[i-1,j] + A[i+1,j] )
        #------------------------------------------
        S1:
            for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
                B[ii, jj] =
                    C0 * ( A[ii,   jj  ] +
                           A[ii,   jj-1] +
                           A[ii,   jj+1] +
                           A[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           A[ii+1, jj  ] )

        #------------------------------------------
        # Sweep 2: Jacobi update from B^t to A^(t+1)
        #   A[i,j] = w * ( B[i,j] + B[i,j-1] + B[i,j+1] + B[i-1,j] + B[i+1,j] )
        #------------------------------------------
        S2:
            for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
                A[ii, jj] =
                    C0 * ( B[ii,   jj  ] +
                           B[ii,   jj-1] +
                           B[ii,   jj+1] +
                           B[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           B[ii+1, jj  ] )

dependencies:
    # 1. Within a given time step t, all S1 updates must complete before any S2 update:
    #    (matches the two separate for-loops in the original C code)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS):
        for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
            S1(t, ii, jj) -> S2(t, *, *)

    # 2. Across time steps, new A produced by S2 at time t is the input A for S1 at time t+1:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        S2(t, *, *) -> S1(t+1, *, *)

    # 3. There are no loop-carried dependencies along ii or jj *within* a sweep:
    #    each point only reads from the previous array (A for S1, B for S2),
    #    and writes to a distinct element in the target array.
    #    This allows full parallelization in the spatial dimensions per sweep.

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Spatial blocking (tiling) to improve cache reuse
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D spatial domain for both sweeps:
    #   - I and J are tile indices
    #   - ii and jj (interior indices) become intra-tile indices
    block(ii, I, TI)      # ii = I * TI + local_ii, tiles of TI rows
    block(jj, J, TJ)      # jj = J * TJ + local_jj, tiles of TJ cols

    # Hoist tile loops to just inside the time loop, so entire tiles are
    # processed for S1, then entire tiles for S2, preserving S1->S2 ordering.
    hoist(I)              # place I as the outermost spatial loop (after t)
    hoist(J)              # place J as next outer spatial loop

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (I, J) tile in a given sweep and time step is independent:
    # we can process tiles in parallel both in S1 and S2.
    # On a 32-core x64 machine, TI×TJ is chosen so that one or a few tiles
    # fit comfortably into L2 / L3 per core.
    parallelize(I)        # distribute tiles across threads
    # (J remains inside I; larger TJ gives good work per tile and contiguous memory)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMD vectorization along the innermost dimension
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # jj indexes contiguous memory (row-major), so we vectorize along jj.
    # VJ should match the hardware SIMD width, e.g., 4 for AVX2 float, 8 for AVX2 double.
    vectorize(jj, VJ)     # emit vector loads/stores and fused adds for stencil in j

    # Optional loop unrolling in j to reduce loop overhead and expose ILP
    unroll(jj, UJ)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic and scalar optimizations
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    #  - The constant weight 0.2 (C0) is hoisted out of all loops.
    #  - Compilers can fuse additions and multiplication into FMA instructions
    #    where available, especially under -O3.
    #  - No change to the mathematical stencil; only the evaluation order within
    #    each sum may change, causing at most benign floating-point roundoff differences.
    hoist(C0)             # ensure 'w' is computed/loaded once outside the time-space loops

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Layout and memory access
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # We *keep* row-major layout for both A and B; the innermost jj loop traverses
    # contiguous elements, yielding:
    #   - unit-stride loads/stores for A[ii,*] and B[ii,*]
    #   - regular strided accesses for neighbors in i (ii-1, ii+1)
    #
    # Changing to column-major would harm the primary access pattern in jj,
    # so we explicitly preserve row-major layout and rely on spatial blocking
    # plus caches to amortize the strided accesses in ii.

    j: dim in [0, N)        # space, column index

    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # used as ping-pong buffer; initial contents unused

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of Jacobi time steps
    omega: DATA_TYPE        # relaxation coefficient, = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tunable performance parameters (chosen w.r.t. cache / SIMD of the target)
    TI: int                 # tile size in i (e.g., 32–256)
    TJ: int                 # tile size in j (e.g., 64–512, multiple of VEC_J)
    VEC_J: int              # SIMD vector width along j (elements)
    UNROLL_J: int           # unroll factor for inner j-loop

computation:
    # 2D Jacobi with 5-point stencil, double-buffered in A and B.
    # Boundary points (i==0, i==N-1, j==0, j==N-1) are never updated.
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):      # time loop must remain sequential
        # Phase 1: B := Jacobi(A)
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S1: B[i, j] =
                    omega * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                              A[i,   j-1] +
                              A[i,   j+1] +
                              A[i-1, j  ] +
                              A[i+1, j  ] )

        # Phase 2: A := Jacobi(B)
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S2: A[i, j] =
                    omega * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                              B[i,   j-1] +
                              B[i,   j+1] +
                              B[i-1, j  ] +
                              B[i+1, j  ] )

optimization:
    # Assumptions:
    # - A and B are distinct, non-aliasing row-major buffers.
    # - N is large so the interior dominates.
    # - N, TSTEPS, omega and tile / SIMD parameters are invariant inside the kernel.

    # 1. Spatial blocking (tiling) over i and j to improve cache locality.
    #    Applied identically to both S1 and S2; boundaries are handled by
    #    clipping tile ranges to [1, N-1).
    block(i, II, TI)        # split i into outer tile index II and inner i
    block(j, JJ, TJ)        # split j into outer tile index JJ and inner j

    # Resulting per-time-step structure (conceptually):
    #   for II                          # tiles of rows
    #     for JJ                        # tiles of columns
    #       for i in tile(II) ∩ [1,N-1)
    #         for j in tile(JJ) ∩ [1,N-1)

    # 2. Loop ordering:
    #    - Keep t outermost and sequential.
    #    - Within each time step, iterate over tiles first (II, JJ),
    #      then intra-tile i, then intra-tile j (unit-stride).
    hoist(t)                # t already outermost; make this explicit
    hoist(II)               # tile rows outside tile columns
    hoist(JJ)               # tile columns outside intra-tile loops

    # 3. Parallelization:
    #    - Within a fixed (t, phase), all (i,j) updates are independent.
    #    - Parallelize on the outer row tiles to reduce scheduling overhead
    #      and balance work across cores.
    parallelize(II)         # distribute II-tiles across threads for S1 and S2

    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling:
    #    - j is the innermost loop and contiguous in memory (row-major),
    #      so vectorize along j.
    #    - Choose TJ as a multiple of VEC_J to minimize scalar remainder work.
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)     # map inner j loop to SIMD lanes
    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)     # unroll j loop within each vectorized chunk

    # 5. Scalar / arithmetic hoisting:
    #    - Keep omega in a register at the innermost level.
    #    - Allow the compiler to use fused multiply-add for omega * sum5.
    hoist(omega)            # load omega once per (t, II, JJ) region (or wider)

domain:
    # Time dimension (Jacobi iterations; each iteration performs two 5-point sweeps)
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # Spatial dimensions restricted to the interior points actually updated
    # (grid is N x N, but i=0, i=N-1, j=0, j=N-1 are fixed boundary values)
    i: dim in [1, N-1)
    j: dim in [1, N-1)

data:
    # 2D grids stored in row-major order (C layout)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Note: memory for A and B is actually allocated for i,j in [0, N),
    # but only interior indices [1, N-1) are written in the kernel.
    # Boundary rows/columns (i=0, i=N-1, j=0, j=N-1) remain at their
    # initialized values and are only read as neighbors.

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid size in each spatial dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of time steps (each step = 2 sweeps)
    w: DATA_TYPE            # stencil weight; w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tuning parameters for optimization (chosen based on hardware/cache)
    TI: int                 # tile size in the i (row) dimension, e.g., 32..256
    VF: int                 # SIMD vector length for j, e.g., 4 or 8
    U: int                  # unrolling factor for j, typically a multiple of VF

computation:
    # For each time step t, perform:
    #   1) A -> B 5-point Jacobi sweep on interior points
    #   2) B -> A 5-point Jacobi sweep on interior points
    #
    # Time steps must execute sequentially because each uses the result
    # of the previous one.
    for t in seq[0, TSTEPS):
        # Sweep 1: read A, write B
        for i, j:
            JACOBI_B(t, i, j):
                B[i, j] =
                    w * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                          A[i,   j-1] +
                          A[i,   j+1] +
                          A[i-1, j  ] +
                          A[i+1, j  ] )

        # Sweep 2: read B, write A
        for i, j:
            JACOBI_A(t, i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    w * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                          B[i,   j-1] +
                          B[i,   j+1] +
                          B[i-1, j  ] +
                          B[i+1, j  ] )

dependencies:
    # Within a given time step t, each interior point (i, j) in sweep 2
    # depends on its 5-point neighborhood in B from sweep 1 of the same t.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i, j:
        # Direct center dependency (neighborhood dependencies are implicit)
        JACOBI_B(t, i, j) -> JACOBI_A(t, i, j)

    # Across time steps, A at time t+1 is produced by JACOBI_A(t, ·, ·)
    # and used as input to JACOBI_B(t+1, ·, ·). This enforces that the
    # outer time loop remains sequential.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1), i, j:
        JACOBI_A(t, i, j) -> JACOBI_B(t+1, i, j)

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Preserve row-major friendly access and innermost j-loop
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The kernel already iterates with j as the innermost loop, which
    # matches row-major storage (elements with consecutive j are contiguous).
    # We keep this structure to maximize spatial locality and enable SIMD.
    hoist(t)  # keep t as the outermost loop (no-op but documented)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization over row tiles (multi-core scalability)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (t, i, j) update within a sweep only reads from the "old" array
    # (A for JACOBI_B, B for JACOBI_A) and writes to the "new" one, so
    # there are no loop-carried dependencies along i or j inside a sweep.
    #
    # We tile the i dimension into blocks of TI consecutive rows and
    # parallelize over the outer tile index. This:
    #   - gives each thread a large, cache-friendly chunk of rows,
    #   - reduces scheduling overhead vs. per-row parallelism,
    #   - maintains correctness because different i-tiles are independent.
    block(i, ii, TI)       # i = ii * TI + (inner i in [0, TI) with bounds clipping)
    hoist(ii)              # loop order: for t, for ii, for i-in-tile, for j
    parallelize(ii)        # run row tiles in parallel for each sweep & time step

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization and unrolling along j
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost j-loop accesses:
    #   A[i, j], A[i, j±1], A[i±1, j]   (or the same pattern on B)
    # which are all at small, fixed offsets. This is ideal for auto-
    # vectorization. We make this explicit and allow the vector width
    # and unroll factor to be tuned.
    vectorize(j, VF)       # map j-iterations to SIMD lanes (e.g., AVX2/AVX-512)
    unroll(j, U)           # unroll j-loop to increase ILP and hide latencies

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic simplifications (kept implicit)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # The expression is already in the form:
    #   tmp = A/B neighbors sum
    #   out = w * tmp
    # so a single multiplication by w per point is required.
    # Modern compilers will:
    #   - hoist the constant w = 0.2 outside loops,
    #   - keep partial sums in registers.
    # No additional arithmetic restructuring is necessary in the model.

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Optional refinement: per-tile software prefetching (comment-only)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # On very large grids where N is much larger than the last-level cache,
    # a further micro-optimization is to add software prefetches for the
    # next rows of A (in JACOBI_B) and B (in JACOBI_A) within each tile ii.
    # This can be modeled as:
    #   #prefetch(A[i+Δ, j]) and #prefetch(B[i+Δ, j])
    # for some small Δ (e.g., 2–4), but is left as an implementation choice
    # rather than a formal directive here.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-03 ---

domain:
    # Time dimension: tsteps outer loop is strictly sequential
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)

    # Space dimensions: N x N grid
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Row-major 2D arrays: contiguous in j
    # index(i, j) = i * N + j
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Only interior points [1, N-1) x [1, N-1) are updated.
    # Boundary values A[0,*], A[N-1,*], A[* ,0], A[* ,N-1] remain as initialized
    # and are read as fixed Dirichlet boundaries throughout the computation.

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid size in each dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of outer iterations
    w: DATA_TYPE            # Jacobi weight, w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) in code

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    TI: int                 # spatial tile size in i (rows), e.g., 32–128
    TJ: int                 # spatial tile size in j (cols), e.g., 32–256
    VEC: int                # vector width for j (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)

computation:
    # For each time step, perform two Jacobi sweeps:
    #  1. B <- stencil(A)
    #  2. A <- stencil(B)
    #
    # Time is strictly sequential to match original semantics and FP behavior.
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):

        # First sweep: compute B from A at time t
        # Matches:
        #   B[i][j] = 0.2 * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][j+1]
        #                    + A[i+1][j] + A[i-1][j]);
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S1_B_from_A(t, i, j):
                B[i, j] =
                    w * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                          A[i,   j-1] +
                          A[i,   j+1] +
                          A[i+1, j  ] +
                          A[i-1, j  ] )

        # Second sweep: compute A from B at the same time step
        # Matches:
        #   A[i][j] = 0.2 * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][j+1]
        #                    + B[i+1][j] + B[i-1][j]);
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S2_A_from_B(t, i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    w * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                          B[i,   j-1] +
                          B[i,   j+1] +
                          B[i+1, j  ] +
                          B[i-1, j  ] )

dependencies:
    # Within a given time step t, each A-update depends on the corresponding
    # B-updates of the same step.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        S1_B_from_A(t, i, j) -> S2_A_from_B(t, i, j)

    # Across time steps, A at step t is the input state for computing B at t+1.
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1), i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
        S2_A_from_B(t, i, j) -> S1_B_from_A(t+1, i, j)

optimization:
    # ---- Spatial blocking (tiling) for cache locality ----
    # We tile i and j so that sub-blocks of A and B fit better into caches.
    # This preserves semantics because tiles are processed in a way that
    # respects the original order within each full sweep.
    block(i, ii, TI)     # i = ii * TI + i_in_tile
    block(j, jj, TJ)     # j = jj * TJ + j_in_tile

    # Keep time dimension outermost; sweeps remain ordered as in original code.
    hoist(t)

    # Apply tiling separately to both sweeps inside each time step:
    #   for t:
    #     for ii, jj: tile of B-from-A
    #     for ii, jj: tile of A-from-B
    #
    # B tiles for a given time step are fully computed (global barrier implied)
    # before any A tiles of that step are used, preserving:
    #   "finish all B updates at t before any A update at t".
    hoist(ii)
    hoist(jj)

    # ---- Parallelization ----
    # Each (i, j) update within a sweep depends only on neighbor values
    # from the *input* grid of that sweep, which is read-only in that phase.
    # Therefore, the spatial loops are safe to parallelize.
    #
    # We parallelize at the outer tile level to:
    #  - amortize thread-management overhead,
    #  - avoid false sharing on adjacent rows/cols,
    #  - map well onto a 32-core CPU (many tiles in flight).
    parallelize(ii)      # distribute tiles of rows across threads
    # Optionally also:
    # parallelize(jj)    # if many cores and large N, 2D tile parallelism

    # Time loop t remains sequential: there are true dependencies between
    # successive timesteps and between S1 and S2 at a given t.

    # ---- Vectorization along j ----
    # j is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), and the stencil
    # in j-direction has unit stride. This is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # ---- Loop unrolling ----
    # Unroll the innermost j loop to:
    #  - expose more ILP,
    #  - reduce loop-control overhead,
    #  - help the compiler schedule loads of neighboring points.
    unroll(j, 4)

    # Optional: mild unrolling in time to increase ILP while respecting
    # sequential time semantics (compiler will emit code for two t-steps
    # inlined, but still ordered).
    unroll(t, 2)

    # ---- Arithmetic hoisting ----
    # The scalar weight w = 0.2 is invariant across all loops.
    # Ensure it is loaded once into a register and reused:
    hoist(w)
    # (This corresponds to computing SCALAR_VAL(0.2) once before
    #  entering the time-stepping loops.)

    # ---- Notes on correctness ----
    # - Boundaries (i = 0 or N-1, j = 0 or N-1) are never written,
    #   exactly as in the original code; they are read as fixed values.
    # - No change is made to the stencil formula or to the ordering
    #   between:
    #       B <- A   and   A <- B
    #   within each time step.
    # - All time steps t are executed in order; no reordering across t.
    # - Parallelization and vectorization affect only independent
    #   (i, j) iterations within each sweep, preserving semantics.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-04 ---

domain:
    # Interior grid points only; boundary rows/cols 0 and N-1 remain unchanged.
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)
    i: dim in [1, N-1)
    j: dim in [1, N-1)

data:
    # Full N×N grids stored in row-major order.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major, includes boundaries at indices 0 and N-1
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major, used as a ping-pong buffer

parameters:
    N: int                  # Grid size (both dimensions)
    TSTEPS: int             # Number of outer loop iterations in the original code
    w: DATA_TYPE            # Relaxation weight; in the given code w = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)
    TI: int                 # Tunable tile size in the i (row) dimension
    TJ: int                 # Tunable tile size in the j (column) dimension
    VEC_WIDTH: int          # Target vector width (elements) for vectorization over j
    UNROLL_J: int           # Unroll factor for inner j loop

computation:
    # Jacobi 2D stencil with two sweeps per outer time iteration:
    #   1) B = J(A)
    #   2) A = J(B)
    # Boundaries of A and B (i=0 or i=N-1 or j=0 or j=N-1) are never updated.

    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        # Sweep 1: read from A, write to B.
        A_to_B:
            for i, j:
                B[i, j] = w * (
                              A[i,   j  ] +
                              A[i,   j-1] +
                              A[i,   j+1] +
                              A[i-1, j  ] +
                              A[i+1, j  ]
                          )

        # Sweep 2: read from B, write to A.
        B_to_A:
            for i, j:
                A[i, j] = w * (
                              B[i,   j  ] +
                              B[i,   j-1] +
                              B[i,   j+1] +
                              B[i-1, j  ] +
                              B[i+1, j  ]
                          )

optimization:
    # --- Scalar and aliasing assumptions ------------------------------------
    hoist(w)
    # hoist(S): treat scalar S as loop-invariant and hoist its load/definition
    # outside all loops that use it. Here, w = 0.2 is a constant; ensure it is
    # computed/loaded once, not per iteration.

    assume_no_alias(A, B)
    # assume_no_alias(X, Y): X and Y do not alias in memory. This matches the
    # benchmark intent and enables better vectorization and reordering.

    # --- Spatial blocking for cache locality --------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D interior domain (i, j) to improve cache reuse within each
    # sweep. Each tile operates on a small sub-block of the grid.
    block(i, ii, TI)
    block(j, jj, TJ)
    # block(d, D, S): replace loop over dimension d by an outer tile loop D and
    # an inner loop over d with tile size S. For example:
    #   for i in [1, N-1)  -->
    #     for ii in [1, N-1) step TI:
    #       for i in [ii, min(ii+TI, N-1))
    #
    # TI, TJ should be tuned so that a tile of A and B plus its 1-cell halo
    # fits comfortably in L1/L2 cache.

    # --- Parallelization -----------------------------------------------------
    parallelize(ii)
    # parallelize(D): iterations along tile dimension D can be executed in
    # parallel (e.g., via OpenMP). Each time-step t is sequential, but within
    # a time-step, tiles in ii are independent in a Jacobi sweep, so they can
    # be distributed across cores on the 32-core machine.

    # To increase parallelism further for very large N, one can also
    # parallelize over jj in addition to ii, as long as the runtime partitions
    # tiles to avoid excessive synchronization:
    # parallelize(jj)

    # --- Vectorization and unrolling ----------------------------------------
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)
    # vectorize(d, W): enforce SIMD vectorization along dimension d with width W.
    # Here, inner j is contiguous in row-major layout, so vector loads/stores
    # for A[i, j±1] and B[i, j±1] are naturally aligned and efficient.

    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)
    # unroll(d, F): unroll loop d by factor F to reduce loop overhead and allow
    # the compiler to better schedule loads, adds, and the final multiply by w.

    # --- Loop ordering -------------------------------------------------------
    # Preserve the original nesting order (t outer, then i, then j) to ensure
    # correctness of the time-dependent stencil and to keep j innermost for
    # vectorization and unit-stride memory access:
    #   t (sequential) -> ii (parallel tiles) -> jj -> i -> j (vectorized)
    #
    # No interchange of t with spatial dimensions is allowed because each
    # time-step depends on the previous one.

    # --- Optional: time-iteration unrolling (purely local) -------------------
    # The outer time loop can be unrolled by a small factor (e.g., 2) to expose
    # more ILP, without changing the number of stencil applications:
    # unroll(t, 2)
    # This preserves semantics because iterations of t are strictly sequential
    # but can still be mechanically unrolled by the compiler.

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      {
	A[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*(j+2) + 2) / n;
	B[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*(j+3) + 3) / n;
      }
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {
      if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_jacobi_2d[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps,
			    int n,
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
			    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,N,N,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j;

#pragma scop
  for (t = 0; t < _PB_TSTEPS; t++)
    {
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  B[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (A[i][j] + A[i][j-1] + A[i][1+j] + A[1+i][j] + A[i-1][j]);
      for (i = 1; i < _PB_N - 1; i++)
	for (j = 1; j < _PB_N - 1; j++)
	  A[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.2) * (B[i][j] + B[i][j-1] + B[i][1+j] + B[1+i][j] + B[i-1][j]);
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_jacobi_2d(tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

    VJ:      int                  # vector width (elements processed per SIMD op), e.g., 4, 8
    UJ:      int                  # unroll factor for j, e.g., 2, 4

computation:
    # Precompute scalar weight once, outside time loop
    C0: w = w

    # Time loop is strictly sequential: each t depends on t-1 via A
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):
        #------------------------------------------
        # Sweep 1: Jacobi update from A^t to B^t
        #   B[i,j] = w * ( A[i,j] + A[i,j-1] + A[i,j+1] + A[i-1,j] + A[i+1,j] )
        #------------------------------------------
        S1:
            for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
                B[ii, jj] =
                    C0 * ( A[ii,   jj  ] +
                           A[ii,   jj-1] +
                           A[ii,   jj+1] +
                           A[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           A[ii+1, jj  ] )

        #------------------------------------------
        # Sweep 2: Jacobi update from B^t to A^(t+1)
        #   A[i,j] = w * ( B[i,j] + B[i,j-1] + B[i,j+1] + B[i-1,j] + B[i+1,j] )
        #------------------------------------------
        S2:
            for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
                A[ii, jj] =
                    C0 * ( B[ii,   jj  ] +
                           B[ii,   jj-1] +
                           B[ii,   jj+1] +
                           B[ii-1, jj  ] +
                           B[ii+1, jj  ] )

dependencies:
    # 1. Within a given time step t, all S1 updates must complete before any S2 update:
    #    (matches the two separate for-loops in the original C code)
    for t in [0, TSTEPS):
        for ii in [1, N-1), jj in [1, N-1):
            S1(t, ii, jj) -> S2(t, *, *)

    # 2. Across time steps, new A produced by S2 at time t is the input A for S1 at time t+1:
    for t in [0, TSTEPS-1):
        S2(t, *, *) -> S1(t+1, *, *)

    # 3. There are no loop-carried dependencies along ii or jj *within* a sweep:
    #    each point only reads from the previous array (A for S1, B for S2),
    #    and writes to a distinct element in the target array.
    #    This allows full parallelization in the spatial dimensions per sweep.

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Spatial blocking (tiling) to improve cache reuse
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the 2D spatial domain for both sweeps:
    #   - I and J are tile indices
    #   - ii and jj (interior indices) become intra-tile indices
    block(ii, I, TI)      # ii = I * TI + local_ii, tiles of TI rows
    block(jj, J, TJ)      # jj = J * TJ + local_jj, tiles of TJ cols

    # Hoist tile loops to just inside the time loop, so entire tiles are
    # processed for S1, then entire tiles for S2, preserving S1->S2 ordering.
    hoist(I)              # place I as the outermost spatial loop (after t)
    hoist(J)              # place J as next outer spatial loop

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (I, J) tile in a given sweep and time step is independent:
    # we can process tiles in parallel both in S1 and S2.
    # On a 32-core x64 machine, TI×TJ is chosen so that one or a few tiles
    # fit comfortably into L2 / L3 per core.
    parallelize(I)        # distribute tiles across threads
    # (J remains inside I; larger TJ gives good work per tile and contiguous memory)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMD vectorization along the innermost dimension
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # jj indexes contiguous memory (row-major), so we vectorize along jj.
    # VJ should match the hardware SIMD width, e.g., 4 for AVX2 float, 8 for AVX2 double.
    vectorize(jj, VJ)     # emit vector loads/stores and fused adds for stencil in j

    # Optional loop unrolling in j to reduce loop overhead and expose ILP
    unroll(jj, UJ)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic and scalar optimizations
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    #  - The constant weight 0.2 (C0) is hoisted out of all loops.
    #  - Compilers can fuse additions and multiplication into FMA instructions
    #    where available, especially under -O3.
    #  - No change to the mathematical stencil; only the evaluation order within
    #    each sum may change, causing at most benign floating-point roundoff differences.
    hoist(C0)             # ensure 'w' is computed/loaded once outside the time-space loops

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Layout and memory access
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # We *keep* row-major layout for both A and B; the innermost jj loop traverses
    # contiguous elements, yielding:
    #   - unit-stride loads/stores for A[ii,*] and B[ii,*]
    #   - regular strided accesses for neighbors in i (ii-1, ii+1)
    #
    # Changing to column-major would harm the primary access pattern in jj,
    # so we explicitly preserve row-major layout and rely on spatial blocking
    # plus caches to amortize the strided accesses in ii.
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-01 ---

domain:
    t: dim in [0, TSTEPS)   # time steps
    i: dim in [0, N)        # space, row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # space, column index

data:

    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # live-in and live-out
    B[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # used as ping-pong buffer; initial contents unused

parameters:
    N: int                  # grid dimension
    TSTEPS: int             # number of Jacobi time steps
    omega: DATA_TYPE        # relaxation coefficient, = SCALAR_VAL(0.2)

    # Tunable performance parameters (chosen w.r.t. cache / SIMD of the target)
    TI: int                 # tile size in i (e.g., 32–256)
    TJ: int                 # tile size in j (e.g., 64–512, multiple of VEC_J)
    VEC_J: int              # SIMD vector width along j (elements)
    UNROLL_J: int           # unroll factor for inner j-loop

computation:
    # 2D Jacobi with 5-point stencil, double-buffered in A and B.
    # Boundary points (i==0, i==N-1, j==0, j==N-1) are never updated.
    for t in seq([0, TSTEPS)):      # time loop must remain sequential
        # Phase 1: B := Jacobi(A)
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S1: B[i, j] =
                    omega * ( A[i,   j  ] +
                              A[i,   j-1] +
                              A[i,   j+1] +
                              A[i-1, j  ] +
                              A[i+1, j  ] )

        # Phase 2: A := Jacobi(B)
        for i in [1, N-1), j in [1, N-1):
            S2: A[i, j] =
                    omega * ( B[i,   j  ] +
                              B[i,   j-1] +
                              B[i,   j+1] +
                              B[i-1, j  ] +
                              B[i+1, j  ] )

optimization:
    # Assumptions:
    # - A and B are distinct, non-aliasing row-major buffers.
    # - N is large so the interior dominates.
    # - N, TSTEPS, omega and tile / SIMD parameters are invariant inside the kernel.

    # 1. Spatial blocking (tiling) over i and j to improve cache locality.
    #    Applied identically to both S1 and S2; boundaries are handled by
    #    clipping tile ranges to [1, N-1).
    block(i, II, TI)        # split i into outer tile index II and inner i
    block(j, JJ, TJ)        # split j into outer tile index JJ and inner j

    # Resulting per-time-step structure (conceptually):
    #   for II                          # tiles of rows
    #     for JJ                        # tiles of columns
    #       for i in tile(II) ∩ [1,N-1)
    #         for j in tile(JJ) ∩ [1,N-1)

    # 2. Loop ordering:
    #    - Keep t outermost and sequential.
    #    - Within each time step, iterate over tiles first (II, JJ),
    #      then intra-tile i, then intra-tile j (unit-stride).
    hoist(t)                # t already outermost; make this explicit
    hoist(II)               # tile rows outside tile columns
    hoist(JJ)               # tile columns outside intra-tile loops

    # 3. Parallelization:
    #    - Within a fixed (t, phase), all (i,j) updates are independent.
    #    - Parallelize on the outer row tiles to reduce scheduling overhead
    #      and balance work across cores.
    parallelize(II)         # distribute II-tiles across threads for S1 and S2

    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling:
    #    - j is the innermost loop and contiguous in memory (row-major),
    #      so vectorize along j.
    #    - Choose TJ as a multiple of VEC_J to minimize scalar remainder work.
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)     # map inner j loop to SIMD lanes
    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)     # unroll j loop within each vectorized chunk

    # 5. Scalar / arithmetic hoisting:
    #    - Keep omega in a register at the innermost level.
    #    - Allow the compiler to use fused multiply-add for omega * sum5.
    hoist(omega)            # load omega once per (t, II, JJ) region (or wider)
--- END OF MODEL: jacobi-2d-02 ---
